title: Representability of the relative morphism functor for algebraic spaces
statement: Algebraic spaces and their morphisms are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], over schemes [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For morphisms of algebraic spaces, flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite presentation means local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness (the diagonal is quasi-compact). Finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; separated means the diagonal is a closed immersion, and universally closed means closed on underlying topological spaces after every algebraic-space base change [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $B$ be an algebraic space over a scheme $S$, and let $Z\to B$ and $W\to B$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces. Assume $Z\to B$ is proper, flat and of finite presentation, and $W\to B$ is separated and of finite presentation. The functor on schemes $U$ over $B$ given by $U\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_U(Z\times_BU,W\times_BU)$ is represented by an algebraic space $M\to B$, locally of finite presentation. Thus its representing bijections are natural in every $U\to B$; the products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

proof.text: Set $A=Z\times_BW$, an algebraic space and a fibre product in the category of algebraic spaces by the current statement of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The projection $A\to Z$ is the base change of $W\to B$, so it is of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], and separated by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. The given properness of $Z\to B$ includes separatedness, as explicitly defined in the locality node; $Z\to B$ is also of finite presentation by hypothesis. Applying the two composition clauses of [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition] to $A\to Z\to B$, we obtain that $A\to B$ is separated and of finite presentation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-hilbert-representability] to $A\to B$ from step 1. It provides an algebraic space $H\to B$ locally of finite presentation representing the closed subspaces $D\subset A_T$ proper, flat and of finite presentation over $T$. The categorical fibre-product assertion of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] identifies $A_T=(Z\times_BW)\times_BT$ with $Z_T\times_TW_T$: in either case a map into this product is a pair of maps into $Z,W$ together with a map into $T$ having the same composite into $B$. The projection-induced identifications and their inverses commute with maps of $T$, since their components do. Thus these are exactly the Hilbert families used by the graph construction, with representing bijections natural on schemes over $B$.

source.place: Tag 0D01, quot-proposition-hilb, applied in the proof of Tag 0D1C.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-graphs-open-in-hilbert], sending $f:Z_T\to W_T$ to its actual graph gives a natural injection $\gamma:\operatorname{Mor}_B(Z,W)\to\mathcal H$. Its image on any scheme test family $D\subset A_T$ is represented by the open $V_D\subset T$ where $\operatorname{pr}_1|_D$ becomes an isomorphism after base change. The hypotheses are precisely properness, flatness and finite presentation of $Z\to B$ and separatedness of $W\to B$; all are given. In particular, no scheme hypothesis on $Z$ or $W$ has been introduced. For a graph in this image, the inverse formula is $\operatorname{pr}_2|_D\circ(\operatorname{pr}_1|_D)^{-1}$.

To work on all $S$-schemes, replace each relative functor $F$ by $T\mapsto\coprod_{b\in B(T)}F(T,b)$, with restriction $(b,x)\mapsto(b|_{T'},x|_{T'})$. Step 2 identifies the total Hilbert functor with $H(T)$. The graph map preserves $b$, so its image defines a subfunctor $M\subset H$. Step 3 identifies its inverse image along every scheme $T\to H$ with the open subscheme $V_D\subset T$. Therefore it is an open subspace of $H$, and is automatically an algebraic space by [def-a1-space-open-subspace]. This argument uses scheme tests, not an assumption that $H$ is a scheme. Give $M$ the structure map $M\hookrightarrow H\to B$. Taking the fibre over a fixed $b:T\to B$ in the total-functor bijection is legitimate because the graph map preserves $b$; its inverse also preserves $b$. Since $\gamma_T$ is injective with this image, this gives bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_B(T,M)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_T(Z_T,W_T)$ for every $T\to B$. They are natural: the Hilbert representing bijections and graph map are natural, so their restrictions to the image and the inverse bijections commute with every test-scheme base change.

source.place: Tag 0D1C, quot-proposition-Mor, the open-subspace inference; spaces.tex lemma-representable-over-space and spaces-properties.tex Tag 03BZ, lemma-open-subspaces.

proof.text: The open immersion $j:M\hookrightarrow H$ is locally of finite presentation: on scheme charts it is an inclusion of an open subscheme, covered near each point by principal affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}R_a\subset\operatorname{Spec}R$, and $R_a\cong R[t]/(at-1)$ has a finite presentation. This verifies the chartwise definition [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], using the scheme-test description in [def-a1-space-open-subspace]. Since $H\to B$ is locally of finite presentation by step 2, the locally-finite-presentation composition clause of [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition] gives that $M\to B$ is locally of finite presentation, as required.
